subject.title: refactor: adopt shared OpenClaw design system

question: Should this PR adopt moving default-branch agent skill updates in a scheduled write-capable workflow, and what credential isolation or policy proof is required before merge?
rationale: The diff changes the repository security and automation boundary by combining write permissions, npm-installed updater code, and mutable external skill guidance; automation should not decide whether that trust model is acceptable.

options.title: Require hardened pinned flow
options.body: Set checkout/read/install phases up without persisted write credentials, keep skills tag-pinned or wait for the approved design-system trust model, and require redacted workflow plus browser proof before merge.

options.title: Accept moving-source updater
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept default-branch skill updates and the broader automation trust model, but should document the security and rollback expectations before landing.

options.title: Split or pause automation
options.body: The static token/style migration can be reviewed separately while the scheduled updater waits for the design-system dependency and security policy decision.

recommendation.title: Require hardened pinned flow
recommendation.body: Set checkout/read/install phases up without persisted write credentials, keep skills tag-pinned or wait for the approved design-system trust model, and require redacted workflow plus browser proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest local human routing signal is recent package/dependency ownership, while the unresolved choice is dependency and scheduled automation policy.
